methodology_notes.market_size_calculation: TAM calculated as sum of middle-market lending ($850B), treasury/cash management ($125B), trade finance ($45B), payment processing ($85B), FX/hedging ($60B), investment banking crossover ($75B), and other commercial services ($55B). Focused on $10M-$3B revenue companies vs. broader SMB market.
methodology_notes.sam_calculation: SAM represents 40% of TAM, targeting companies with international operations or multi-state presence in Citi's 17 US markets + 6 international expansion markets. Excludes pure-play domestic SMBs better served by regional banks and mega-corporates ($3B+ revenue) served by corporate/investment banking.
methodology_notes.som_calculation: SOM represents 14% of SAM, based on Citi achieving 12-14% middle-market share over 3 years from current ~6%, leveraging international differentiation and doubling commercial banking revenue from $3B to $6B.
methodology_notes.citi_market_share: Estimated at 5.8-6.7% of middle-market segment based on 14,000 core commercial clients + expansion to ~450,000 total including small/mid-market. Cross-referenced with $3B commercial banking revenue and $87B Banking segment loans.
methodology_notes.data_quality: Primary sources: Citigroup 10-Q/10-K, investor presentations, press releases. Middle-market estimates synthesized from industry reports (Mordor Intelligence, CSI Market) and peer comparisons. International banking rankings from public disclosures.
methodology_notes.limitations: Exact middle-market segment size by individual bank not publicly disclosed; Citi position estimated from 14K commercial clients, revenue, and loan balances. TAM components involve estimates where exact figures unavailable. Post-restructuring impact on US commercial banking still evolving through 2025-2026.
